insight.title: Why Small Choices Make Big Decisions Harder
insight.subtitle: How tiny decisions drain the focus you need for important work

sections.text: You spend ten minutes picking a coffee or a font, then feel exhausted when it’s time to sign a contract. Your brain treats every choice as a withdrawal from the same limited account.

This is your decision-making engine at work. It doesn't distinguish between the color of a slide and the direction of a company. Each minor selection adds friction, slowly grinding your judgment to a halt.

By the time you reach high-stakes moments, your clarity is gone. High-performers don't just have better judgment; they have fewer things to judge, preserving their mental energy for the moments that actually matter.
Try this today: When you face a trivial choice today, pick the first decent option in under five seconds.
Quality of thought is determined by the energy you refuse to waste on things that don't matter.

news.title: US-China AI race must strike a balance between security and openness
news.description: The United States House Select Committee on China recently released a report on artificial intelligence. Titled “Buy What It Can, Steal What It Must: China’s Campaign to Acquire Frontier AI Capabilities”, it captures a hardening view in Washington that Beijing’s artificial intelligence rise is closely tied to both market access and security concerns. Whether fully substantiated or not, such beliefs are increasingly shaping the policy lens through which technology competition between the two...
news.why: New AI rules change how your personal data is protected online.

news.title: Europe should focus on own security as global threats mount, Dutch intelligence agency says
news.description: THE HAGUE, April 21 - Europe must take greater responsibility for its own security, the Dutch military intelligence agency MIVD said on Tuesday, citing pressure on long-standing Western alliances and China's support for Russia's war in Ukraine.
news.why: Higher defense spending leads to fewer funds for local public services.

news.title: Russia's Sergei Shoigu says safety of Russians in Transnistria under threat, TASS reports
news.description: ⁠The ​safety of ​Russian citizens in Moldova's breakaway Transnistria ​region ‌is currently ⁠under threat, ‌Sergei Shoigu, secretary of Russia's Security ​Council, said on Tuesday. Speaking on FRANCE 24, Laurențiu Pleșca, Policy Fellow at the German Marshall Fund, explains that Russia is using the same playbook it used in eastern Ukraine and Donbas adding that "it's remarkable that Shoigu is not even trying to hide it".

news.title: US warns it will run out of money to pay airport security workers in coming weeks

news.why: You will face longer security lines during your next airport visit.

news.title: Indonesia passes law to protect domestic workers after a wait of over 20 years
news.description: Indonesia’s parliament passed a law on Tuesday to protect the rights of domestic workers after more than two decades of deliberations and multiple delays. The bill was first introduced in 2004 to protect the country’s 4.2 million domestic workers, almost 90 per cent of them women, according to data from the Ministry of Manpower. They were previously not legally classified as workers, meaning they were forced to operate in an informal and unregulated economy, exposed to exploitation and...
news.why: Hiring household help now requires formal contracts and higher wages.
